summary: Audited all 19 assigned HVAC/appliance/meter blog pages via full-file reads; wrote complete per-page audit table + LEGACY REBUILD LIST to .squad/SQ-065/wave1/mason-pages.md (verified: file exists, 20,513 chars). Evidence: ac-running has 15 <h2> + 7 <h3> + 4 internal <a> links; aux-heat has 9 <h2> + 10 <h3>; duct-leaks has 4 {{< ref }} links. The automation that flags 'legacy' pages is unreliable and will keep mislabeling strong pages as thin.

Actual render bugs found (fix immediately): aux-heat-vs-emergency-heat-meaning has two broken/malformed H2s — line 45 shows '<h2 id="the-problem">The problem: \' (stray backslash, truncated label) and line 96 shows '<h2 id="emergency-heat">What Emergency Heat means (and when it' (truncated, no closing tag). gas-vs-electric-heating-cost-comparison has a nested-bracket markdown link near the top: '[For more detail, see our guide to [heat pump savings](/blog/48-heat-pump-vs-gas-furnace-savings/).]' which renders as broken/fugly HTML.

Genuinely weak page (below 6/10): gas-vs-electric-heating-cost-comparison (quality 6, seo 6) — only 1 source (DOE policy post), HTML table/headings, cost table uses 95% furnace while sibling 48-heat-pump uses 96% AFUE in its breakeven math (cross-page contradiction), and ends with a single link to the generator page. Recommend merge into 48-heat-pump-vs-gas-furnace-savings with redirect.

Strongest pages (keep, minimal work): why-is-my-furnace-blowing-cold-air (9/9, CPSC+IRS sourced, fresh 25C credit note), duct-leaks-symptoms (9/8, mastic-vs-duct-tape quote, arithmetic-labeled table), ductless-mini-split-vs-central-air (9/8, verified SEER2/HSPF2 anchors + Mass Save data), 48-heat-pump-vs-gas-furnace-savings (9/9, robust formula + sourcing), what-merv-rating (9/8), drafts how-to (9/8), 47-check-energy-leaks (9/8).

Cross-page number contradictions: (1) AFUE benchmark inconsistency — gas-vs-electric uses 95% furnace, 48-heat-pump uses 96% AFUE; (2) electric-rate vintages differ across pages but are correctly labeled by date (18.4¢ vs 17.45¢/18.34¢); (3) standby figures differ between phantom-power (32–87W pre-standard, 51.5W modern) and 47-check (67W LBNL) — different sources, should cross-note; (4) SEER2/HSPF2 figures are consistent across ductless-mini and 48-heat-pump; (5) wattage examples consistent (1500W×3h=4.5kWh; 1500W×8h≈$2.20/day); (6) 25C credit consistently dated as ended 12/31/2025 in three pages.
Pages rated below 6/10: none (lowest is gas-vs-electric at 6/6; aux-heat and heat-pump-running at quality 6 but SEO 8/7).
